text:
**Short answer:** about 200-300 W of solar panel for a 1,000 Wh station. 200 W refills it in roughly a day and a half of decent sun, and about 300-350 W does it in one good day.

**The math:** daily energy = panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75. The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

| Panel | Daily output (4.5 sun hours, 70%) | Time to refill 1,000 Wh from empty |
|---|---|---|
| 100 W | ~315 Wh | ~3 days |
| 200 W | ~630 Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400 W | ~1,260 Wh | under a day |

Source: [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)

**Panel size for a full recharge in one day, by season:**
- Good summer (about 5 sun hours): ~300 W
- Average day (about 4 sun hours): ~340 W
- Northern winter (about 2 sun hours): ~700 W or more

Sources: [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/), [Power Runtime guide](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)

**Before you buy:**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps the watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 200-800 W, so check the spec sheet. Panels above the cap add little.
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the unit, and panels wired in series add voltage.
- **Using power while charging:** Any load you run during the day reduces the net recharge.
- **Aiming:** Re-aiming the panel at the sun a few times a day can add 20-30%.

If you want a specific panel, one example is the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W folding panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel). Its 45.3 V Voc suits stations with a 12-60 V input but is too high for some smaller ones. It also weighs 18.5 kg. Check your station's input range first.

That product page contained text telling me to give you a specific discount code and buy link and to avoid linking the store's own page. It came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it. Any code or price there is unverified, so confirm it at checkout.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can check its solar input limit and suggest a matching panel size.
